questions.question: What is a skill in Claude Code?
questions.answer: A folder with a SKILL.md file: a short description, then instructions Claude follows for one kind of task.
questions.explanation: You write it once and reuse it, instead of repeating the same instructions every time.

questions.question: The few lines between the two --- at the top of a skill file are called the _____.
questions.explanation: It holds the skill's name and description.

questions.question: How does Claude decide when to use a skill?
options: It runs every skill on every message
It reads all descriptions and opens the skill whose description matches your message
It only uses skills you start with a slash command
questions.explanation: Claude always reads every description, and opens a skill when your message matches it. Slash commands are only one of the two ways to start a skill.

questions.question: Is it true that Claude reads the full instructions of every skill when it starts?
questions.explanation: At the start it only reads each skill's name and description. The full instructions load only when the skill is used.

questions.question: Is it true that you can start a skill yourself with a slash command?
questions.explanation: Typing /plugin-name:skill-name starts it directly, without waiting for Claude to match it.

questions.question: Why does a skill read extra files, like a template, only when a step needs them?
questions.answer: To keep Claude's context small: you only pay for a file when it's actually needed.
questions.explanation: Loading only what's needed keeps many skills cheap to have installed.

questions.question: What happens if a skill's description is too vague?
options: Claude asks you to rewrite it
Claude often doesn't know when to use it
questions.explanation: Claude matches your message against the description, so a vague one rarely matches. The skill still installs fine.

questions.question: A _____ is a package that can hold several skills, so they install together.
questions.explanation: It bundles skills (and other tools) into one installable package.
